newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU wheat tax not very likely at season end - source.
newsitem.headline: EU wheat tax not very likely at season end - source.

text.p: The European Union is "not very likely" to restore a tax on wheat exports as the 1996/97 (July/June) season draws to an end, a European grain industry source said on Thursday.
"It is not very likely at the end of the campaign," the source said.
The tax that still applied to wheat exports at the start of the 1996/97 season was aimed at limiting exports in the early stages of the campaign, he explained.
The European Union restored subdidies on wheat exports in mid-September 1996.
"Now it is different, we are at the end of the season," he said.
Some exporters, notably those who still had uncovered business, were worried that the EU might decide to restore a tax on exports in the face of volatile prices.
Earlier this week the EU moved to scrap fixed daily refunds on wheat grain and flour exports, replacing them with a nil value refund that cannot be set in advance.
The nil value refund leaves traders exposed to a tax, should the EU decide to impose one.
"The market is very tense. People are nervous," the source said.

On Wednesday the head of France's grain office ONIC, Alain Moulinier, said that world price levels did not currently justify restoring a tax on soft wheat exports although this could not be ruled out in the future if prices were to head higher.
